notice: Traceability is design evidence. Linked tests are not live test execution results. Use the CI run or local pytest report to establish a passing build.

requirements.title: Deny access without an authenticated session
requirements.control: Bearer session checked on protected requests; idle and absolute expiry

requirements.title: Limit clinical access to role and care relationship
requirements.control: Deny-by-default RBAC plus assignment or patient-scoped emergency grant

requirements.title: Detect altered, deleted, or rolled-back audit records
requirements.control: AES-GCM authentication, sequence/hash chain, authenticated anchor, off-host checkpoints

requirements.title: Withhold evidence when verification fails
requirements.control: All new evidence paths use the shared verifier before releasing content

requirements.title: Require a meaningful emergency justification
requirements.control: Trim before length validation; record the reason and limit the grant duration

requirements.title: Record accountable emergency-access reviews
requirements.control: Immutable review events, verified projection, reviewer identity and optimistic revision check

requirements.title: Explain suspicious activity using source events
requirements.control: Documented thresholds and event-sequence evidence; no unvalidated AI risk score

requirements.title: Export filtered, verified evidence safely
requirements.control: Auditor authorization, audit-first export, snapshot head and count, CSV formula neutralization

requirements.title: Reject invalid patient registration data
requirements.control: Calendar-valid birth date, trimmed required fields, unknown fields rejected

requirements.title: Keep generated secrets private and out of Git
requirements.control: Fresh installation keys; restrictive POSIX permissions or Windows DACLs; ignored generated state

threats.scenario: Attacker reuses or guesses a session credential
threats.mitigation: Random tokens, hashed token storage, expiry, account lockout
threats.residual: MFA and enterprise SSO are deferred

threats.scenario: IT administrator or unassigned staff requests clinical data
threats.mitigation: Server-side role and relationship checks on every request
threats.residual: Legitimate emergency access still needs human review

threats.scenario: Disk attacker changes ciphertext, deletes records, or restores a complete old host snapshot
threats.mitigation: GCM tags, chain, anchors and independently retained checkpoints
threats.residual: Whole-host rollback requires a checkpoint beyond the restored state

threats.scenario: Staff denies using an emergency override or auditor silently overwrites a review
threats.mitigation: Authenticated grant/review events, reviewer identity, immutable history
threats.residual: Recorded justification can be dishonest; investigation remains necessary

threats.scenario: Repeated authentication failures exhaust resources or storage
threats.mitigation: Account lockout and visible repeated-failure findings
threats.residual: Reverse-proxy rate limiting and disk quotas are production requirements

threats.scenario: Unauthorized export or spreadsheet formulas execute when opened
threats.mitigation: Auditor-only verified export, audit trail, CSV text neutralization
threats.residual: Downloaded reports require secure handling and retention policy

threats.scenario: Whitespace-only names, invalid dates, or unexpected fields cross the API boundary
threats.mitigation: Typed request models, normalization before validation, explicit field allowlists
threats.residual: A valid value is not proof of real-world accuracy

threats.scenario: Generated root keys are copied from a repository or read by another local account
threats.mitigation: Fresh generated keys, ignored runtime state, restrictive file permissions
threats.residual: Previously published keys remain compromised in old Git history

architecture.name: Encrypted audit store
architecture.detail: Per-record AES-GCM · one-way key ratchet · authenticated head

architecture.name: Independent checkpoint
architecture.detail: Auditor-side sequence and head hash · rollback evidence

demo.title: Establish normal access
demo.action: Open P-1001. Clinical data is visible because the doctor is assigned.

demo.title: Demonstrate least privilege
demo.action: Open P-1002 three times. Clinical data stays restricted; the auditor findings explain the repeated denials.

demo.title: Use accountable emergency access
demo.action: Enter an emergency reason on P-1002 and choose Break glass. Reopen the clinical record.

demo.title: Close the review loop
demo.action: Open Emergency reviews, inspect the justification, then mark reviewed or flag for investigation.

demo.title: Anchor the evidence
demo.action: Publish a checkpoint and note its sequence and hash.
demo.evidence: Auditor-side checkpoint and console CHECKPOINT event

demo.title: Detect a controlled modification
demo.action: Run python scripts/demo_lab.py. It creates its own temporary store and demonstrates tampering without changing the running hospital.
demo.evidence: Clean verification followed by a failed authentication tag check

demo.title: Deliver verified evidence
demo.action: Filter the evidence by patient, download JSON or CSV, and inspect the snapshot head and audit record.

demo.title: Trace the engineering decisions
demo.action: Open Engineering, inspect the STRIDE model and requirements, then use the policy simulator to compare roles.
